newsitem.title: USA: UAW, Chrysler reach tentative pact.
newsitem.headline: UAW, Chrysler reach tentative pact.

text.p: Chrysler Corp and the United Auto Workers announced on Sunday night they reached a tentative labour accord that guarantees hourly jobs and offers the same economic package the union set with Ford nearly two weeks ago.
"We're done here at Chrysler," UAW President Stephen Yokich said at a press conference at Chrysler headquarters.
Yokich and Chrysler Chairman Robert Eaton would not release details of the agreement, which still requires ratification by Chrysler's 66,000 UAW members.

But Yokich said the Chrysler agreement is patterned after the Ford contract, which offers major pension improvements, a $2,000 lump sum payment in the first year and three percent base wage hikes in the second and third years.
Chrysler assembly line workers now make an average of $19 an hour.
The pact means that General Motors Corp is the last member of the U.S. Big Three automakers still working without a new agreement. The previous agreement expired September 14.

Industry analysts have said Chrysler could easily afford the job security provisions of the Ford contract, but that a similar pact could cause problems for GM, which needs to shrink its work force to cut costs to competitive levels.

The agreement with Ford, reached September 16, guarantees employment for 95 percent of the company's 105,000 UAW workers during the life of the three-year deal. The last of Ford's UAW locals were expected to ratify the agreement on Sunday.
"I think this is has got to be a first in our history," Yokich said. "As Ford finishes their voting today, we finished at Chrysler as well."
Eaton declined to comment on whether the company accepted restrictions on outsourcing, the practice of contracting work out to outside suppliers.
"(The negotiations) produced very, very good results -- results that are good for our employees, yet something we can definitely live with," he said.

The Chrysler contract is scheduled to be voted on Thursday by the UAW-Chrysler council, made up of plant-level representatives. Yokich said he did not know when a ratification vote would be finalised.
Yokich also did not specify when talks at GM will pick up. Talks continued at the subcommittee level this weekend at GM.
"I hope you see me with (GM Chairman) Jack Smith very soon," he said.

Meantime, with little more than three days before a strike deadline, GM and the Canadian Auto Workers (CAW) union remained at odds over work by outside contractors and other issues, union officials said.

The union chose GM Canada on Monday as its second negotiating target after reaching agreement with Chrysler Canada earlier this month. The Chrysler pact, ratified last weekend, halts plant sales and closings during the three-year agreement and commits Chrysler to replace any union jobs lost due to work done by outside contractors.
